summary.headline: IndusInd Bank Q2 FY27 PAT rose to Rs.1,242 crore and RoA to 0.87%, helped by FCNR(B) inflows of USD 3.51 billion.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed a sharp recovery: deposits and advances returned to double-digit YoY growth (10% and 11%), and asset quality improved across sub-segments with gross NPA at 2.73% and net NPA at 0.83%. Profit after tax reached Rs.1,242 crore against a normalised Rs.824 crore in Q1. Margins compressed to 3.23% (from a normalised 3.35%) due to FCNR(B) mobilisation, and management said it expects some deposit-rate uptick in H2. Management reiterated a 1% exit RoA ambition for FY27 and a medium-term 175-180 bps historical RoA benchmark.

financial_highlights.change: up 51% QoQ vs normalised Rs.824 crore; vs loss a year ago
CET1 down about 40 bps QoQ per analyst question

segments.name: Retail deposits and FCNR(B)
segments.commentary: USD 3.51 billion FCNR(B) mobilised under RBI swap window (about 2.75% market share); Affluent and NRI deposits about Rs.1,05,000 crore, up 23% QoQ. CDs cut to 3.3% of deposits from 5.9% QoQ.

segments.name: Vehicle Finance
segments.commentary: Book Rs.1,00,651 crore, up 5% YoY and 1% QoQ; disbursements Rs.11,968 crore, up 17% YoY and 10% QoQ. Annualised net slippages 1.67%.

segments.name: Rural / Micro-loans (BFIL)
segments.commentary: Micro-loan book grew 8% QoQ to Rs.17,571 crore after about eight quarters of decline; annualised net slippage 2.2%. Merchant Finance Rs.8,694 crore, up 20% YoY.

segments.name: Consumer loans (ex-FCNR(B))
segments.commentary: Book Rs.59,776 crore, up 7% QoQ; home loans up 39% YoY to Rs.7,733 crore. Credit card and personal loan books fell 3% and 2% QoQ respectively.

segments.name: Wholesale Banking
segments.commentary: Loan book up 10% QoQ and YoY; Commercial & Mid-Market up 13% QoQ. Fee income Rs.446 crore, up 37% YoY and 9% QoQ; gross slippage annualised 0.07%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 exit RoA ambition of 1%; management said progress is clear, and historical RoA was 1.75-1.80% (medium-term ambition), with no comment on FY28.
Expects advances growth to be in line with market; YoY base effect as loan book de-grew in last two quarters of FY26.
Plans to add 100+ bank branches in H2 FY27.
Expects H2 retail growth to lift asset yields; management expects to recoup part of 12 bps NIM drop over next two quarters.
Recurring credit cost expected at 5-6 bps; one-time ECL transition impact about 1.1% of loans pretax (as clarified on call).
Expects some uptick in deposit rates in H2 as rate hikes and liquidity tightening are anticipated.
capex_capacity: Added 124 outlets in Q2, primarily within BFIL; plans 100+ bank branches in H2 FY27 in underpenetrated geographies.
Added about 4,300 employees at bank level, largely sourcing roles.
Six voice bot programs launched; twelve more customer and employee journeys identified in roadmap.
Capital raise: enabling provision in place; will look at a capital raise at an appropriate time.
demand_pricing: Deposits grew 10% YoY and advances 11% YoY; average advances ex-FCNR(B) up 6% QoQ, and 9% QoQ including FCNR(B)-related loans.
Retail assets grew 12% QoQ overall, 4% QoQ excluding FCNR(B)-related lending.
Loan yields fell about 25 bps QoQ, mainly due to FCNR(B) leverage book and wholesale mix; management said ex-FCNR yields only marginally lower.
Fee income improved across retail and wholesale; management said core fee (about 1.35% of assets) is sustainable with no major one-offs.
Bancassurance income Rs.960 crore in FY26 (about 15% of fee income); draft IRDAI norms could have material impact, too early to quantify.
Micro-loan drought-related stress flagged in Karnataka, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh; portfolio quality still strong.

qa_highlights.question: Will loan growth catch up with system growth, given it trails?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said YoY comparisons are distorted by FY26 de-growth; YTD Q1 book grew 4-5%. It expects to grow in line with market in H2.

qa_highlights.question: ECL transition impact and recurring credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: One-time impact is about 1.1% of loans pretax (not 1.5-1.7%); recurring credit cost 5-6 bps.

qa_highlights.question: FCNR(B) impact on NIM and cost of deposits outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FCNR impact is about 7-8 bps by analyst estimate but holistic view makes isolation complex; cost of deposits may rise as rate hikes are expected before March.

qa_highlights.question: Fee income sustainability and one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: One-offs about INR100 crore (INR48-50 crore AFS/HTM sale gains plus FX sales); trading income about INR70 crore; core fees improving across retail and wholesale.

qa_highlights.question: Savings account weakness and CASA strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding NRI outflows to FCNR(B), SA would be roughly flat; new-to-bank accounts up 12% QoQ to about 3.6 lakh; focus on granular SA in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Tier 1 decline of 55 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to balance sheet growth and higher market risk RWA; RWA density stable at 73%.

risks_watch: FCNR(B) leverage book with short-term foreign currency borrowings not fully hedged on tenure basis; management says FX gaps are within Board NOOP limits.
Deposit cost pressure from expected rate hikes and tightening liquidity in H2; CASA share declining and SA down 5% QoQ.
Possible bancassurance income hit from draft IRDAI commission norms.
Microfinance and rural stress from drought in parts of Karnataka, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh, and state elections.
CET1 consumption (about 40 bps QoQ) and potential capital raise timing.
Unsecured book (credit cards and personal loans) still shrinking QoQ.
summary.management_tone: Confident on momentum and profitability, with a cautious tone on the macro: management repeatedly flagged fuel prices, drought, rate hikes and liquidity tightening. It was evasive on FY28 RoA guidance and on quantifying the FCNR(B) margin impact, and said capital-raise timing will be decided later.
key_quotes: Q2 RoA improved to 0.87%, compared with a normalised 0.63% in Q1, despite temporary margin pressure from FCNR(B) mobilisation.
So therefore, the focus really is to go in the second half of the year is to grow SA on a much more granular basis.
We will look at a capital raise at an appropriate time.

adds.what: 100+ bank branches planned in H2 FY27 in underpenetrated geographies

growth.why: Management guides loan growth in line with market (advances up 11% YoY, 9% QoQ incl. FCNR-related loans) and a 1% exit FY27 RoA ambition, backed partly by 100+ branches planned for H2 FY27, FCNR(B) mobilisation of USD 3.51bn, and expected H2 retail yield uplift; no specific order or capacity numbers beyond branch count.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects H2 retail growth to lift asset yields and to recoup part of the 12 bps NIM drop from 3.35% normalised, but deposit-rate uptick is a headwind.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management plans 100+ bank branches in H2 FY27 in underpenetrated geographies, after adding 124 outlets in Q2, primarily within BFIL.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 11% YoY and guidance is growth in line with market, with YTD Q1 book growth of 4-5% and micro-loans up 8% QoQ after eight quarters of decline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capital raise is enabled by a provision but timing is undecided; CET1 fell about 40 bps QoQ to 15.55%, with no utilisation metric applicable to a bank.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 RoA rose to 0.87% from 0.63% and management is making clear progress on the 1% exit RoA ambition, but no upgrade was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Deposit-cost pressure from expected H2 rate hikes and a 12 bps NIM drop to 3.23%, plus drought stress in micro-loans and bancassurance risk from draft IRDAI norms.

rows.label: Asset quality improvement
rows.why: GNPA fell to 2.73% and NNPA to 0.83% with PCR at 70%, and recurring credit cost is guided at 5-6 bps, while provisions fell 54% YoY to Rs.1,223 crore.

rows.label: One-time ECL transition impact
rows.why: One-time ECL transition impact is about 1.1% of loans pretax (lower than the 1.5-1.7% feared), which management clarified on the call.

rows.label: Draft IRDAI bancassurance norms
rows.why: Bancassurance income was Rs.960 crore in FY26 (about 15% of fee income), and draft commission norms could have a material impact that is too early to quantify.

tone.note: Management was confident on momentum, RoA progress and asset quality, but cautious on macro (fuel, drought, rate hikes, liquidity) and evasive on FY28 RoA, FCNR(B) margin impact and capital-raise timing; analysts pushed on loan growth lag, ECL impact, NIM, CASA and Tier 1 decline.

oneOffs.what: Q1 FY27 base was a normalised Rs.824 crore PAT; reported Rs.1,242 crore PAT is up 51% QoQ and vs a loss a year ago, so the YoY comparison is flattered by a weak year-ago base rather than a one-off gai
About Rs.100 crore of fee one-offs (Rs.48-50 crore AFS/HTM sale gains plus FX sales) in Q2 non-interest income of Rs.2,248 crore
Provisions down 54% YoY to Rs.1,223 crore; year-ago quarter was disrupted by an FY26 loss, so profit comparison is against a low base

quality.why: Deposits (+10% YoY) and advances (+11% YoY) growth is volume-led, but a large part of the headline profit rise is flattered by a weak year-ago base (loss, provisions down 54% YoY), and about Rs.100 crore of fee one-offs plus an FCNR(B) inflow-driven loan book sit inside the quarter's numbers.
